nodes.description: Without a functional TRAP complex, nascent glycoproteins entering the ER are less efficiently N-glycosylated, so some sequons are left unoccupied. This is a type I (assembly/transfer) defect, measurable in patient fibroblasts with a glycosylation reporter and in serum as reduced glycan-site occupancy of transferrin. In knockout cell lines the defect is most pronounced under ER stress and partly adapts over time, which may help explain why serum transferrin is often only marginally abnormal.

nodes.description: In patient fibroblasts, loss of SSR4 lowers the levels of the other TRAP subunits, and re-expressing wild-type SSR4 partially restores them. The generality of this is contested: in CRISPR knockout clones of the A549 cell line, loss of SSR4 did not eliminate the other subunits (SSR2 was the subunit that stabilised the others). Both results are recorded.
